handoff.purpose: Contains tail of _remove_tree_no_follow, public wrapper remove_tree_no_follow, and GitWorktreeManager class with init and several methods.

symbols.name: _remove_tree_no_follow
symbols.note: Tail of function; handles reparse points, directories, and files; raises WorktreeRemovalRace.

symbols.name: remove_tree_no_follow
symbols.note: Public wrapper delegating to _remove_tree_no_follow; exists to avoid importing private function.

symbols.name: GitWorktreeManager
symbols.note: Manages isolated Git worktrees; includes init, property, and several methods.

symbols.name: GitWorktreeManager._alloc_file
symbols.note: Returns allocation file path based on SHA256 hash.

symbols.name: GitWorktreeManager._record_allocation
symbols.note: Writes allocation record before git worktree add.

symbols.name: GitWorktreeManager._reach_chain
symbols.note: Returns list of paths from worktree_root to target.

symbols.name: GitWorktreeManager._refuse_if_repo_adjacent
symbols.note: Raises error if candidate is within repo_path or vice versa.

symbols.name: GitWorktreeManager._refuse_if_the_primary_checkout_moved
symbols.note: Mitigation against checkout move attack; docstring contains extensive claims.

claims.text: Deliberately delegates rather than being aliased, so a test that monkeypatches _remove_tree_no_follow also intercepts this path.
claims.why: Function body calls _remove_tree_no_follow directly, so monkeypatching _remove_tree_no_follow will affect this call.

claims.text: The ONLY thing :meth:`reap_branches` is allowed to act on.
claims.why: reap_branches method not present in this chunk.

claims.text: Process memory is the one store the candidate cannot reach
claims.why: Refers to trust model not shown in this chunk.

claims.text: Compared again before every unattended recursive delete -- see _refuse_if_the_primary_checkout_moved.
claims.why: _refuse_if_the_primary_checkout_moved is defined in this chunk and exists for that purpose.

claims.text: CALIBRATED AT CONSTRUCTION, deliberately: it records whatever is there and later demands only that it be UNCHANGED.
claims.why: self._repo_ancestor_identity is assigned in __init__ with list of (parent, identity) pairs.
Call to _record_allocation before git worktree add is not shown; only the method definition.

claims.text: Ordering matters for crash-safety: anything that can exist on disk must already have a record, otherwise a crash mid-``add`` leaves a directory that cleanup would (correctly, but uselessly) refuse forever.
claims.why: No evidence of the ordering in this chunk.

claims.text: Step 3 of :meth:`_require_allocated_worktree` checks this chain once, before the decision; :func:`_remove_tree_no_follow` re-checks it on every directory it opens, because 'checked once, before' is exactly the stale classification that let a repository be deleted.
claims.why: _require_allocated_worktree not present in this chunk; re-check in _remove_tree_no_follow not shown.

claims.text: A MITIGATION, NOT A CLOSURE. ... Every containment check then passes honestly ... and the whole checkout is destroyed with cleanup returning success (measured, this box, 3/3).
claims.why: No code evidence of the attack or measurements; only documentation.

claims.text: 1. ``repo_path`` MUST NOT BE A REPARSE POINT. ``__init__`` calls ``.resolve()``, so a legitimate ``repo_path`` is a fully resolved real directory and can never be one; if it is one now, something put it there.
claims.why: The .resolve() call is not visible in this chunk; __init__ is partially shown but the assignment to repo_path is not fully detailed.

claims.text: 2. THE LEAF IDENTITY, no-follow. Catches the decoy that is a real directory (a fresh ``mkdir`` at the vacated name), which check 1 cannot see.
claims.why: Leaf identity check (likely _path_identity) not shown in this chunk.

claims.text: 3. THE ANCESTOR IDENTITIES, no-follow, calibrated at construction. Catches the same attack one component up ... Measured before this check existed: 40/40 work files destroyed, leaf identity matching, both stat and lstat agreeing, cleanup raising only ``NotADirectoryError`` after the damage.
claims.why: Ancestor identity check and measurements not shown in this chunk.

claims.text: WHAT IT DOES NOT CATCH... * anything ELSE the candidate moves in ... * a move performed AFTER this check and before the walk reaches it. * a filesystem with no ``st_ino``. * the case where the candidate moves the checkout in and then restores something at the old path with the SAME identity.
claims.why: These are limitations stated in documentation; no code in this chunk addresses them.

observations.what: The function _remove_tree_no_follow has a long comment block explaining design decisions about reparse points and directory removal order. No new code beyond line 600.
remove_tree_no_follow is a thin wrapper that delegates to _remove_tree_no_follow, as documented.
GitWorktreeManager.__init__ sets _repo_identity and _repo_ancestor_identity using _path_identity and _lexical, but the exact behavior of _path_identity is not shown.
The docstring for _refuse_if_the_primary_checkout_moved contains extensive claims about attacks and measurements that cannot be verified from this chunk alone.
The method _run_git uses subprocess.run with shell=False (default) and capture_output=True. It raises RuntimeError on failure.
Allocation methods use SHA256 hashing on _key(worktree_path) to create filenames, and store JSON records with schema version.
